title: bee herding run reads herdr lifecycle state the way herdr defines it
action: Fix the three places run.rs misreads herdr's agent lifecycle state. Read CONTEXT.md first — it quotes herdr's published contract verbatim and locks D1, D2 and D3; do not re-derive them. (1) TRAIT SEAM. `Herdr::agent_prompt` at line 363 is `fn agent_prompt(&self, job_id: &str, prompt: &str) -> Result<(), String>` and `RealHerdr`'s impl at lines 498-500 shells `herdr agent prompt <job_id> <prompt>` with no wait flags. Widen it so the caller can ask herdr to observe the submission: pass an `until` state and a timeout in milliseconds, and have `RealHerdr` emit `herdr agent prompt <job_id> <prompt> --wait --until <state> --timeout <ms>`. herdr refuses a submission that produces no observed lifecycle change within 5000ms with `agent_prompt_stalled`; classify that reply into a distinct typed outcome the caller can branch on (mirror the shape of `is_pane_busy_error` at lines 733-735 — a small predicate over herdr's error string is the house style here), separate from an ordinary transport error. Add a `Herdr` method for herdr's own settled-state wait, `herdr agent wait <job_id> --until idle --until done --timeout <ms>`, and give `FakeHerdr` (line 1812) and `PanicHerdr` (line 1950) their matching impls; `FakeHerdr` needs configurable results for both so the tests can drive stalled, blocked and ready outcomes without a process. (2) READY GATE — D2. `wait_for_agent_ready` at line 811 returns true only on `Some("idle")`. Accept `idle` OR `done`: herdr states that `done` is the same underlying ready-for-input state for a tab that has not been seen in the focused UI, that CLI reads never mark a tab seen, and every pane this verb splits carries `--no-focus` — so `done` is the normal resting state of a bee worker pane and idle-only rejects a pane that is ready. Keep the check-then-sleep shape, the injected `now`/`sleep` seams, and the 60s `ready_wait_secs` at line 291 exactly as they are. (3) DELIVERY — D1. `deliver_pointer` at line 783 sends the pointer up to `POINTER_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` (30) times and treats an agent-caused transition into `working` as the receipt. That transition test is satisfied by the agent's own BOOT flap, which is how job trust-par-2 recorded a delivery into a pane that never rendered the pointer. Retire the baseline/transition poll: send once through the widened `agent_prompt` with `--wait --until working` and a timeout, and let herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` BE the delivery failure, returned at once with a message that names the job, the pane and what stalled. KEEP the `result_present()` escape — an ultra-fast round that writes its result before any status observation still counts as delivered. A bounded retry may stay for a transport error, but never for a stall and never 30 blind sends into a booting TUI. Update the three call sites at lines 1208-1215, 1353-1360 and 1484-1491 and leave their `SpawnFailed` mapping and pane-lifecycle rules alone. (4) BLOCKED — D3. herdr's `blocked` means it recognized an approval or question UI. Today run.rs never reads that state anywhere. Make it a fast, loud failure at all three wait points: the ready gate, the delivery, and `decide_poll` at line 604 (which today only escapes the idle timeout through `find_limit_match`/`LIMIT_PATTERNS` at lines 61-73 and 624-627). A `blocked` observation ends the wait immediately with a typed error naming the pane id, the tail of its pane text (reuse `pane_read`, line 373), and the remedy — answer the prompt in that pane, or pre-authorize whatever it is asking so the agent stops asking. Never burn the 60s ready wait, the resends, or the idle timeout on a question nobody is going to answer. Do not add any agent-specific pattern table for trust prompts: `blocked` is the whole mechanism. Leave `LIMIT_PATTERNS` and the paused-limit path working as they are.

truths: The ready gate accepts a pane reporting done, not only idle
A blocked pane ends the ready wait, the pointer delivery and the round poll at once, with an error naming the pane and the remedy
Pointer delivery is one herdr-observed submission whose stall herdr reports, not a bee-observed transition into working
An ultra-fast round whose result file appears before any status observation still counts as delivered

artifacts.substantive: widened agent_prompt seam with a typed stall outcome, an agent-wait seam, idle-or-done ready gate, herdr-observed delivery, blocked fast-fail at three wait points, and the FakeHerdr/PanicHerdr impls plus rewritten and new tests; no TODO stubs

key_links: RealHerdr::agent_prompt emits --wait --until --timeout and classifies agent_prompt_stalled distinctly from a transport error
prohibitions: No agent-specific trust-prompt or approval-prompt pattern table — blocked is the mechanism
No change to LIMIT_PATTERNS, find_limit_match, or the paused-limit path
No change to the pane-close rules, the dispatch/wave-ledger rows, or the --dry-run path
Do not drop the result_present() delivery escape
